thread:
pranay: Quick sync — we need to lock down TLS profiles across regions and produce an inventory + action checklist. Target EOD Fri. Thoughts?

sarah: +1. Do we want min TLS1.3 only? Any clients still on TLS1.2?

mikael: We have a handful in APAC that still speak TLS1.2 — payment-proxy and legacy-ingest (ap-south-1). I'll post the list.

mikael: legacy-ingest -> ingress-gw-ap-south, payment-proxy -> lb-pp-apac

sarah: We should not force-terminate without RBAC/KMS path planned. Rotator roles need update: `roles/keystore.unwrap` and `roles/keystore.wrapFallback` — make sure principle-of-least-privilege.

pranay: Agreed. Action items: 1) Inventory by EOD, 2) RBAC mapping for KMS unwrap/wrap, 3) Audit log schema for handshakes/unwraps, 4) Canary + rollback plan.

eva: For audit logs, we need handshake metrics and KMS unwrap events. Suggested fields: `cert_thumbprint`, `peer_cn`, `kek_wrap_id`, `unwrap_result`, `region`, `request_id`. Ship to `tls-handshakes` index.

mikael: Also include `cipher_suite`, `client_hello_version`, `sni` and `latency_ms`. We'll tag with `service_owner` so we can slice by team.

pranay: Who owns RBAC changes? @sarah take lead? @mikael you own inventory. @eva audit schema. I'll coordinate rollout windows with infra.

sarah: I can own RBAC. Question: are we changing IAM in central KMS or per-region? Prefer central with region-scoped bindings to simplify audits.

mikael: Central is ideal but APAC compliance requires local control for some tenants. Plan for central by default, region exceptions in a controlled allowlist.

rotator-bot: rotator scheduled cert sync for eu-west will run at 2026-03-25T02:00Z — automated notice.

sarah: Reminder: any RBAC changes must be reviewed in security-preprod and have a staging canary (single region, low-traffic service). No global flip without rollback tested.

pranay: Triage note: if KMS unwrap fails during rollout, fallback should route to `fallback-keystore` in-region and return a 502 to callers with header `x-tls-fallback: true`. That lets upper layers surface a controlled degradation.

eva: For incident response — create an alert: if `kms.unwrap_error_rate > 0.5%` for 5m then page oncall + security. Also surface `handshake_latency` and `stapling_missing` counts.

mikael: I'll attach the inventory CSV later. For sampling, I'll run: \n```\nopenssl s_client -connect ingress.example.com:443 -servername ingress.example.com | sed -n '1,20p'\n```\nand also curl TLS info: `curl --tlsv1.3 -sI https://ingress.example.com` to validate profiles.

sarah: Add OCSP stapling check to ingress healthcheck — if stapling absent mark as `degraded` and warn 1 hour before rollout.

pranay: Also confirm cipher whitelist: prefer AEAD suites (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256). Drop RC4/3DES and CBC legacy.

eva: Audit schema draft: will add example event JSON and field mapping by Thu. Will also include retention/PII guidance.

mikael: Inventory ETA: Thu EOD. I'll include per-region notes and any legacy clients that need staggered migration.

sarah: RBAC PR ETA: Thu late afternoon — will include a canary plan and a reviewer list (security, infra, platform).

pranay: Rollout window proposed: Sat 0200-0600 UTC (low traffic). Rolling by region with 30m observation windows.

eva: Add to checklist: audit pipelines validated, dashboards (error rate, unwrap latency), and playbook for escalations.

mikael: One more: coordinate with support — customer-facing services should get a pre-rollout banner and support runbook for observed 502s.

sarah: Noted. Also ensure KMS policy change is staged with IAM change-approval logs (audit log must show who approved).

pranay: I'll compile into a short playbook and open a PR in docs/tls-hardening with the checklist: Inventory / RBAC mapping / Audit schema / Canary plan / Rollout window / Rollback runbook.

sarah: +1. ETA for PR? Fri 5pm PT.

mikael: Inventory will be uploaded by Thu EOD.

eva: Audit schema draft by Thu.

pranay: Thanks — ping me if blockers. :thumbsup:
